text:
jess: Hey team, escalating on behalf of AcmeSearch — their embedding calls started returning 400s with a "dimension mismatch" error this morning after a model rollover. Also seeing spikes in tail latency when batch_size > 16. Can someone help triage?

kim: ack. can you paste the exact error and a minimal repro?/request id would help too.

jess: Error payload we get from the API: 
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": { "message": "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 768 but got 384", "code": "INVALID_ARGUMENT" }
}
```
curl we used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"acme-sim-2","input":["hello world"]}'
```
Request id header returned: x-request-id: a1b2c3d4-7890

raul: that error screams model vector-dim changed (acme-sim-2) vs what the client expects. Did they pin a model version earlier?

jess: They said they didn't pin the model and we did a silent model swap yesterday (acme-sim-1 -> acme-sim-2) which upgraded dims from 384->768. Customer's vector DB expects 384-length vectors.

kim: ah — that explains 400s. But what's the latency spike with larger batches? any traces?

jess: We captured traces for a failing batch run. Span names from the trace (trace id t-0a9f): 
- embeddings.route.dispatch
- embeddings.batcher.wait
- model.infer.kvcache_lookup
- model.infer.forward
- network.egress

For batch_size=32 the embeddings.batcher.wait time increases a lot (tail > 700ms) and model.infer.forward is also higher due to sequence padding mismatch on that model.

opsteam: sharing the quick observability checklist:
1) verify which model instance served the request via /models endpoint and model metadata (dim).
2) check per-request latency breakdown on the Embeddings Route dashboard (per-route spans + p50/p95/p99).
3) pull the specific trace via trace id.

jess: I tried: `GET https://control.redwood.ai/v1/models/acme-sim-2` returns metadata: `{"vector_dim": 768, "quantized": false, "variants": ["acme-sim-2"]}`. Customer's DB was onboarded with acme-sim-1 (dim 384).

dataplane-bot: incident created: INC-45321, severity P2. Assigned: support -> kim, runtime -> raul.

kim: For immediate mitigation we can:
- advise customer to pin to acme-sim-1 if still available OR
- return a compatibility error with clear message and link to docs OR
- offer an interim adapter that resizes vectors client-side (lossy) as a stopgap.
Which do they prefer?

jess: They want lowest friction. They asked for a rollback if it's quick. Are old model variants still available?

raul: Check list: if acme-sim-1 artifact still in model-store and routing table has a variant entry, we can temporarily route their org to the older variant via a per-customer routing policy. I'll check routing state now.

[~2m later]

raul: routing table shows acme-sim-1 is still available for 12h in the artifact store. I can create a per-tenant routing override. That should stop the 400s immediately and remove conversion work.

jess: please proceed, also can we fix the latency/batcher issue independent of rollback? customer reported that when they batch on their side to 64 they hit timeouts.

raul: two likely causes for batch latency:
- model variant now has longer hidden-size -> more compute per token -> added infer time when batch is large.
- our batcher scheduling uses grouping by sequence length; if the new model increases tokenization length or uses different padding rules, padding blowup increases compute.

kim: to debug per-request latency we need metrics from the Embeddings Route dashboard: p50/p95/p99 for span names above, plus `batcher.queue_time` histogram and `model.forward_ms`. Can you export the last 1h for trace t-0a9f and a few successful/failed requests?

jess: attached snippet of logs for request a1b2c3d4-7890: 
```
[2026-03-08T09:12:31Z] INFO request=start id=a1b2c3d4 route=embeddings org=acme
[2026-03-08T09:12:31Z] DEBUG batcher.enqueue id=a1b2c3d4 batch_id=b-422 size=32 wait_ms=48
[2026-03-08T09:12:31Z] DEBUG batcher.dequeue batch_id=b-422 size=32 scheduler=round_robin
[2026-03-08T09:12:31Z] INFO model.forward id=a1b2c3d4 model=acme-sim-2 gpu=0 forward_ms=520
[2026-03-08T09:12:31Z] ERROR request=fail id=a1b2c3d4 error=embedding_dim_mismatch expected=768 got=384
```
kim: forward_ms=520 for a single batch is high but not impossible. Combined with wait_ms and serialization/egress we're over timeout for some clients. Suggestations:
- tune batcher.max_batch_size and batcher.max_wait_ms for that org (lower max_batch_size when caller times out).
- enable our adaptive batching which groups by seq_len to reduce padding.
- add a guard in the API gateway to detect client-side expected dim via header `X-Expected-Vector-Dim` and fail-fast with actionable message.

jess: customer-side change is hard because they use a managed DB. For short term, raul will rollback routing for them. For medium term: add a dashboard panel to show per-org model vector_dim mismatches and per-org batcher timeouts. Can someone file a metrics/dashboard ticket?

opsteam: I'll open a ticket: OPS-2127. Dashboard panels to include:
- per-tenant embeddings.batch_wait_ms p50/p95/p99
- per-tenant model.forward_ms p50/p95/p99
- count of `embedding_dim_mismatch` errors by org per hour
- trace link quick column (x-request-id -> trace)

kim: also add an alert: if embedding_dim_mismatch errors > 5 in 10m for an org, auto-create P1 and block new model rollouts for that org until resolved.

jess: sounds good. Raul, please confirm rollback and then we'll message the customer with incident details and ETA.

raul: rollback complete for org=acme, routing override in place. Verified with a successful embedding call pinned to acme-sim-1: response vector len=384.

jess: customer notified, they're back to green. Thanks. Follow-ups:
- ops to add dashboard (OPS-2127)
- api to add header guard (ENG-4921)
- docs to add guidance on pinning models / vector-dim compatibility (DOCS-884)

support-bot: ticket INC-45321 updated: status=mitigated, owner=raul, notes=rollout override applied.

kim: closing loop — we should add a runbook entry to support playbooks for vector-dim breakage. I'll draft and post to #support-playbooks.

jess: thanks everyone.
